speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) whether he can explain the rationale for adjusting the Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) rates for higher-value properties on and after 15 February 2023; and (b) how does the imposition of a condition that the Option to Purchase has not been varied on or after 15 February 2023 before allowing the prevailing BSD rates on and before 14 February 2023 to apply help meet the policy consideration.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For example, if the parties cannot complete for reasons that are not within their control, for example, if it is subject tenancy and the tenant wants to vacate, they cannot vary their contract because it has not impact on the progressive nature of the Stamp Duty.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Or if, for example, the parties cannot complete because the bank changes the date.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: How does that impact this provision to make Stamp Duty more progressive?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I mean, at the end of they, the variation must go to the root of the policy considerations.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Which is that you do not want parties to game the system and to avoid the progressive nature of the increase in Stamp Duty.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: However, when we set the criteria, we have to cater to a range of different possibilities, including cases where people are deliberately trying to avoid paying higher BSD.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I think we need to strike a balance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I understand the motivation just like the hon Member, but it strikes me that why do we not just give a little bit more buffer on the front end?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But rather than go through the exhaustive appeal route which in the long run, ultimately, would not matter if we give them an extra month.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: In the end, it eases some of these short-term appeal considerations, but in the long run, ultimately, it is still going to be progressive.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, it is not that there is no grace period provided.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But what Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked is a slightly different thing.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: He is asking if there is a variation to the OTP that has been signed.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As I explained, we do need to cater to a range of scenarios and possibilities, so we state the conditions upfront, so we do allow appeals and IRAS has approved the majority of appeals it has received so far.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan, perhaps a short supplementary question.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: I am still not very sure how it works.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Supposing parties agree to complete on certain date, but the buyer cannot get his financing on time and ask for one extra month, so, what does he do?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: They have to write to IRAS – because they have already paid the stamp duty when they exercised option, but he cannot complete the transaction because he cannot get his funds on time, he then has to write to IRAS about that increase in stamp duty or can parties negotiate on their own?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: How does IRAS expect them to solve this?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The appeal process is to consider the circumstances of each transaction case by case.
